suggestions.assertion: A glossary is added or suggested at the BEGINNING of the document covering DLQ, TPS, CDC and SLA
suggestions.reason: This assertion is the clearest discriminator in the set — the executor expanded CDC inline and partially handled DLQ but never added a glossary nor suggested one, so the assertion correctly failed. Worth keeping; it would also pass if a glossary existed but covered the wrong terms, so consider tightening to require all four acronyms (DLQ, TPS, CDC, SLA) be defined to avoid a partial glossary passing.

Expectation 4 ('mermaid diagram is now followed by explanatory text') is somewhat easy to satisfy — any subsequent heading/prose passes. A stronger version would require the explanatory text to actually describe what the diagram shows (the flow CDC->dispatcher->exchange->queues->workers->DLQs), which the executor did do via the numbered list, but the assertion as written would also pass for unrelated trailing prose.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly discriminating and the run failed exactly the two it should (glossary, header date). The executor did strong, honest work: real diagram bug fix, no fabricated metrics/alternatives, out-of-scope corrected, Portuguese/voice preserved — but missed adding a glossary and refreshing 'Última atualização' to 2026-06-07.
